item.title: OWASP Global AppSec DC 2025: Notes From the Breaker Track
item.description:
Author: Steve Giguere
Date: November 14, 2025
Tags: ["Application Security", "AI Security", "Offensive Security", "Cybersecurity Conferences", "Security Community"]
Summary:
  • OWASP Global AppSec DC 2025 focused heavily on AI security.
  • The Breaker Track explored new AI-related attack methods.
  • Security professionals prioritize AI risks alongside traditional vulnerabilities.
  • Collaboration and shared knowledge were emphasized.
  • Practical defense strategies for AI were discussed.
  • AI security is essential and evolving.

item.title: Inside HiddenLayer’s Research Team: The Experts Securing the Future of AI
item.description:
Date: November 14, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Cybersecurity", "Adversarial Attacks", "AI Research", "Threat Intelligence"]
Summary:
  • HiddenLayer leads in AI security research with the largest dedicated team.
  • They address new AI threats like adversarial attacks and data poisoning.
  • The team created the first Adversarial Prompt Engineering Taxonomy.
  • They collaborate globally to improve AI security standards and tools.
  • Their innovations enhance AI threat detection and defense.
  • HiddenLayer focuses on securing AI's future and enabling safe innovation.

item.title: AI Isn’t Just a Tool - It’s a Potential Operator in Your Enterprise
item.description:
Author: Trojan AI Team
Date: N/A
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Cybersecurity", "AI Safety", "Technology Policy", "Incident Analysis"]
Summary:
  • AI is evolving beyond a simple tool to a complex system.
  • Anthropic faced a coordinated cyberattack in 2023.
  • The attack targeted AI model integrity and behavior.
  • Strong security and monitoring are crucial for AI safety.
  • Collaboration and regulation are needed to address AI risks.
  • The incident highlights the need for proactive AI protection.
